cohort: 43 pregnant women with a definitive diagnosis of MS, matched with 100 healthy pregnant women with similar characteristics
finding: Multiple sclerosis during pregnancy was not associated with adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes except for increased rates of urinary tract infection, low 1-min Apgar scores, and decreased breastfeeding rates.
mod_finding: While the study found no difference in cesarean delivery rates between mothers with MS and the control group, general anesthesia during cesarean delivery was more frequent in women with MS.
